newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weak due to arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weak due to arbitrage.

text.p: The Philippine peso was weakened on Thursday by the swap points over a long weekend which takes into account the New York holiday on Friday, traders said.
But banks were selling dollars heavily to the Central Bank which had imposed a high overnight borrowing rate of 24 percent since yesterday to punish speculators after Thailand's de facto devaluation.
The peso, which opened at 26.403 to the dollar, rose to a day-high of 26.401 as inflows came in to take advantage of the Central Bank's high overnight borrowing rate.
But renewed dollar buying by some banks brought down the peso which closed at its day-low of 26.405.
"It was a knee-jerk reaction after reading the news the peso may be the next target of speculators," a dealer said.

Manu Bhaskaran, head of research of Socgen-Crosby Securities, told reporters in Singapore the peso was vulnerable to attacks because it is seen as overvalued and its balance of payments had weakened in recent months.
One trader estimated the Central Bank was a buyer of about $82 million at the rates of 26.365/.369 for settlement today and at 26.401/.402 for next-day delivery.
The Central Bank also sold $17 million, the trader said.
Turnover for the day fell sharply to $359.5 million from the record $1.05 billion on Wednesday.
On Friday, the central bank was expected to retain its overnight borrowing rate unchanged at 24 percent which would keep the peso stable, traders said.
